svg.title: Class entry requirements
svg.desc: Table for Classes A, B, C, D, E and G showing ATC clearance and radio, transponder and ADS-B Out, and pilot certificate requirements exactly as the PHAK text states them. Only requirements the text states are shown.
svg.text: Class entry requirements as PHAK states them
Shows what the handbook text states. The full rules are in 14 CFR part 91 (Figure 15-9); check them
with your instructor.
Class
What the text states
A
IFR only, and only under an ATC clearance received before entering.
Two-way radio able to talk with ATC on a frequency assigned by ATC (unless otherwise authorized).
Transponder as in 14 CFR 91.215 unless otherwise authorized by ATC.
ADS-B Out (91.225 airspace) from January 1, 2020.
B
ATC clearance required for all aircraft.
Operable two-way radio able to talk with ATC on the frequencies for that Class B area (unless
authorized otherwise).
Transponder with automatic altitude reporting, 91.215(a), unless authorized by ATC.
ADS-B Out (91.225 airspace) from January 1, 2020.
Pilot certificate: To take off or land: private pilot certificate; or recreational (61.101(d)) or sport
(61.325) with their requirements; or a student meeting 61.94 (and 61.95 as applicable).
C
Two-way radio contact with ATC established before entering and kept up while inside.
Departing a tower airport: contact the tower. Departing a satellite airport with no tower: contact ATC
as soon as practicable.
Transponder, 91.215, unless authorized by ATC.
ADS-B Out (91.225 airspace) from January 1, 2020.
D
Two-way radio contact with ATC established before entering and kept up while inside.
Departing: same rule as Class C (tower, or ATC as soon as practicable from a satellite airport with no
tower).
E
No clearance or entry radio rule stated. Near an airport, follow the Class G requirements and any 14
CFR part 93 traffic pattern.
Airport with an operating control tower: radio contact is needed within 4 NM of the airport, up to and
including 2,500 ft AGL.
ADS-B Out (91.225 airspace) from January 1, 2020.
G
ATC has no authority or responsibility to control traffic here, so no clearance.
VFR minimums apply.
Other lines in the text: in Class C and D, no one may take off or land at a satellite airport except in line
with FAA arrival and departure traffic patterns. Radio failure at a tower airport under VFR: land if weather is
at or above basic VFR minimums, visual contact with the tower is kept and a landing clearance is received.
